My publications span mechanistic systems biology, angiogenesis, physiological
modeling, biomedical devices, biomaterials, and computational methods.

The selected publications below represent the central development of my
mechanistic modeling research.

[View my Google Scholar profile](https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=LM9WspQAAAAJ&hl=en){.btn .btn-primary}

## Selected mechanistic modeling publications

::: {.project-card}

### Mechanistic computational model of HIF signaling

**Oliveira, R. H. M., Pathak, A. P., & Popel, A. S. (2026).**  
*A mechanistic computational model of the HIF signaling pathway.*  
**iScience, 29**(6), 116195.

This study developed a mechanistic model of hypoxia-inducible factor
signaling to investigate the regulation and dynamics of cellular responses
to hypoxia.

[View publication](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.isci.2026.116195){.btn .btn-outline-primary}

[Explore project](projects/hif-signaling.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}

### HGF-VEGF signaling in endothelial cells

**Oliveira, R. H. M., Patil, A., Annex, B. H., Pathak, A. P., & Popel, A. S. (2025).**  
*Mechanistic computational model of HGF-VEGF mediated endothelial cell
proliferation and vascular permeability.*  
**iScience, 28**(8), 113199.

This work integrated HGF and VEGF signaling to investigate endothelial-cell
proliferation and vascular permeability under conditions relevant to
angiogenesis and vascular disease.

[View publication](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.isci.2025.113199){.btn .btn-outline-primary}

[Explore project](projects/hgf-vegf-signaling.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}

<span class="project-tag">HGF</span>
<span class="project-tag">VEGF</span>
<span class="project-tag">Angiogenesis</span>

:::

::: {.project-card}

### Notch-Dll4 signaling and endothelial patterning

**Oliveira, R. H. M., Annex, B. H., & Popel, A. S. (2024).**  
*Endothelial cells signaling and patterning under hypoxia: a mechanistic
integrative computational model including the Notch-Dll4 pathway.*  
**Frontiers in Physiology, 15**, 1351753.

This study used an integrative mechanistic model to investigate how
Notch-Dll4 and other pro-angiogenic signals regulate endothelial-cell
patterning under hypoxia.

[View publication](https://doi.org/10.3389/fphys.2024.1351753){.btn .btn-outline-primary}

[Explore project](projects/notch-dll4.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}

<span class="project-tag">Notch-Dll4</span>
<span class="project-tag">Endothelial cells</span>
<span class="project-tag">Hypoxia</span>

:::
